questions.stem: Why does the equation \(y^2 = -3\) have no real solution?
options: The square of any real number is always zero or positive, so negative numbers have no real square roots.
Because 3 is a prime number and cannot be divided by 2.

questions.hint: Think about what happens when you square a positive number, zero, or a negative number. Can y × y ever be negative?

keyPoints.note: Positive × positive = positive, and negative × negative = positive.

steps.explain: Test squaring a positive number: \((+) \times (+) = (+)> 0\).
Test squaring zero or a negative number: \(0^2 = 0\), and \((-) \times (-) = (+) > 0\).
Therefore, for every real number \(y\), \(y^2 \ge 0\), so \(y^2\) can never equal \(-3\).
Hence, negative numbers have no real square roots, so \(y^2 = -3\) has no real solution.
